title: Sylow reduction of a finite torsion module
statement:
Let $G$ be profinite, $\ell$ a prime, and $M$ a finite
$\ell$-primary discrete
continuous $G$-module. There is an open subgroup $H\subset G$
of index prime to $\ell$ such that $M|_H$ has a finite filtration
whose successive quotients are trivial $\mathbf F_\ell$-modules.

proof.text: For every $m\in M$, continuity for the discrete action means its stabilizer is open [def-exc-continuous-cohomology]. Since $M$ is finite, the intersection $K$ of all these stabilizers is open; it is the kernel of $G\to\operatorname{Aut}(M)$ and hence normal. Therefore $Q=G/K$ is finite (the open cosets cover the compact group $G$, so finitely many suffice), and the action factors through $Q$. This includes $M=0$, for which $Q$ is trivial.

source.place: Lemma 0A3R (lemma-pullback-filtered), proof, image of the continuous monodromy action in Aut(V) is finite; the finite-module case is stated again in Lemma 0GJ0 (lemma-pullback-filtered-modules), proof

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-sylow-subgroup-prime-index] to the finite group $Q$ to obtain an $\ell$-Sylow subgroup $P$. Let $H$ be the inverse image of $P$ under $G\twoheadrightarrow Q$. It is open, since it is a union of cosets of the open kernel $K$, and $G/H\cong Q/P$ as finite sets. Thus $[G:H]=[Q:P]$ is prime to $\ell$; the restricted action of $H$ factors through the finite $\ell$-group $P$.

source.place: Lemma 0A3R (lemma-pullback-filtered), proof, selection of the Sylow subgroup and prime-to-ell index

proof.text: Since $M$ is finite and $\ell$-primary, some $n\geq0$ satisfies $\ell^n M=0$ (take a maximum of the finitely many elementwise exponents; $n=0$ when $M=0$). Put $M_j=\{m\in M: \ell^j m=0\}$ for $0\leq j\leq n$. Then $0=M_0\subseteq M_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq M_n=M$ is a finite $P$-stable filtration: $\ell^j(pm)=p(\ell^jm)=0$. Every $M_{j+1}/M_j$ is finite and killed by $\ell$, because $\ell m\in M_j$ whenever $m\in M_{j+1}$. It is therefore a finite-dimensional $\mathbf F_\ell[P]$-module. Zero quotients require no further filtration.

source.place: Lemma 0GIZ (lemma-action-l-group), statement for modules killed by a power of ell; explicit exponent filtration supplies the needed finite abelian-group case

proof.text: For each nonzero quotient $V_j=M_{j+1}/M_j$, apply [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-l-group-filtration] to its $P$-action. This yields a finite chain of $P$-stable subspaces from $0$ to $V_j$ with trivial one-dimensional $\mathbf F_\ell$ quotients. Pull the subspaces back along $M_{j+1}\twoheadrightarrow V_j$, obtaining a chain from $M_j$ to $M_{j+1}$; the quotient of consecutive inverse images is canonically the corresponding quotient of subspaces, because their common kernel is $M_j$. Concatenate these chains for $j=0,\ldots,n-1$ and delete repeated terms. The result starts at $0$, ends at $M$, is $H$-stable because $H$ acts through $P$, and has exactly the claimed trivial $\mathbf F_\ell$ successive quotients. For $M=0$ it is the one-term chain $0=M$.

split_report.summary: The finite continuous action factors through its finite image. An ell-Sylow subgroup gives an open inverse image of prime-to-ell index by the existing Mathlib leaf. The explicit annihilator-by-ell-power filtration has finite F_ell[P] quotients; the existing Lean-closed finite ell-group representation theorem filters each nonzero quotient. Inverse images and concatenation give the asserted filtration. The zero module and zero intermediate quotients are included. No new node is needed.

The Stacks source is 0A3R/0GIZ.

lean.statement: theorem exists_openSubgroup_primary_module_filtration (G : Type u) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalGroup G] [CompactSpace G] [T2Space G] [TotallyDisconnectedSpace G] (ℓ : ℕ) (hℓ : ℓ.Prime) (M : DiscreteContinuousRep.{0, u, v} ℤ G) [Finite M.obj.V] (hM : IsPGroup ℓ (Multiplicative M.obj.V)) : ∃ H : OpenSubgroup G, H.toSubgroup.index.Coprime ℓ ∧ ∃ (n : ℕ) (F : Fin (n + 1) → AddSubgroup M.obj.V), Monotone F ∧ F 0 = ⊥ ∧ F (Fin.last n) = ⊤ ∧ (∀ (i : Fin (n + 1)) (g : H) (x : M.obj.V), x ∈ F i → M.obj.ρ (g : G) x ∈ F i) ∧ (∀ (i : Fin n) (x : M.obj.V), x ∈ F i.succ → ℓ • x ∈ F i.castSucc ∧ ∀ g : H, M.obj.ρ (g : G) x - x ∈ F i.castSucc)
lean.note: Uses the landed discrete continuous module category over ℤ (abelian groups), rather than requiring a choice of finite coefficient ring. The quotient conditions are the exact elementwise criteria for annihilation by ℓ and trivial H-action; no dimension restriction is imposed.
